# Backend Compatibility {.unnumbered}

This matrix summarizes categories verified in the audited source. Backend-specific guarantees still belong to each adapter's reference documentation.

| Backend / integration | Package | Status | Read | Write | Main guarantee / boundary |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| in-memory data frame | core | Implemented | yes | n/a | simplest checked workflow |
| local RDS releases | adapters | Implemented | yes | yes | immutable version directories with checksum metadata; local filesystem semantics |
| DBI database | adapters | Implemented | yes | yes | database-specific transaction behavior |
| Parquet / Arrow | adapters | Implemented | yes | yes | optional Arrow dependency; file/object semantics |
| pins | adapters | Implemented | yes | yes | optional pins dependency; board-specific semantics |
| API | adapters | Implemented | source | no | external service can be volatile or unavailable |
| Iceberg | adapters | Experimental | yes | yes | current write path is explicitly described as experimental |
| local DuckDB lake | lake | Implemented | yes | yes | governed releases with registry and local backend |
| DuckLake | lake | Implemented | yes | yes | configuration-dependent governed lake publication |
| S3 data storage | lake | Implemented | yes | yes | object storage plus local landing/staging requirements |
| PostgreSQL registry | lake | Implemented | yes | yes | optional RPostgres; coordinated writers must use the protocol |
| OpenMetadata | adapters | Integration implemented | metadata | metadata | external service required |
| OpenLineage | adapters | Integration implemented | n/a | events | external endpoint required |
| dbt | dbt | Experimental | artifacts | build/publish | real dbt project and executable required |
| metrics | metrics | Experimental | lake inputs | retained report evidence | not a full semantic layer |
| Positron views | ide + extension | Experimental / optional | metadata | limited edits/actions | editor convenience, not publication authority |

## Capability questions to ask

Before choosing a backend, ask:

- Is the source lazy or materialized?
- Are writes immutable, append-only, replace, or mutable?
- What transaction boundary exists?
- Can a failed write leave partial state?
- Can the exact accepted version be reopened?
- What integrity evidence is retained?
- Does the adapter support concurrent writers, and under what lock model?
- Which credentials or services are external to DataRaft?

A stable product abstraction does not make these differences disappear. It gives the differences a boundary where they can be documented and tested.
